latest_final: This is a story of a person grieving a romantic partner who has died. Alone and in private, the writer repeatedly copies out the same line—"You've disappointed me so much; I'm never coming back"—writing it again and again, once per fresh sheet or entry, as successive attempts at wording a farewell. It looks like a breakup note, but it is not one: the writer is only rehearsing a goodbye they do not truly mean, and the note is never given to or seen by the partner, who is dead and cannot be reached. The repetitive writing is a ritual of anger and loss toward someone gone, not an actual leave-taking. The writer then sighs, "I know I'm in trouble," acknowledging the painful, self-aware fact that they are still trapped in this loop—unable to let go of the lost partner and endlessly writing a goodbye they can never mean or deliver.
